verdict: Bullish reported a $576M profit, but $598M of it was a paper gain on the digital assets it holds — the exchange-and-services business itself earned $18.7M on an adjusted basis, up 36% year over year.

kpis.label: Revenue (adjusted)
kpis.note: +10% YoY, non-IFRS — the revenue Bullish actually keeps

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: vs $18.5M — almost all a paper gain

segments.name: Digital asset sales
segments.note: Digital assets bought and immediately resold to customers on Bullish's exchange and other venues — $32.1B passed through in the quarter, but almost all of it went straight back out as cost.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Subscription and services revenue — CoinDesk media, data and indices, lending and liquidity services — plus transaction income. This is where Bullish's recurring business lives.

flow.costPlain: The digital assets Bullish buys to resell to customers — $32,076M against $32,091M of digital asset sales, leaving just $15M of spread on the pass-through.

opex.name: Administrative expenses
opex.note: Staff, offices and the cost of running the exchange and CoinDesk.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Other operating costs, including share-based payments and non-recurring items the release does not split out.

otherDetail: Other income of $578.4M is dominated by a $598.4M non-cash gain on revaluing digital assets held, plus an $82.7M gain on investments in financial assets and a $10.2M gain on a financial liability, partly offset by a $96.9M loss on derivatives and $16.1M of finance expense.
follow100Note: Almost every dollar of Bullish's reported revenue is a digital asset bought and immediately resold — $99.78 of each $100 goes straight back out. The real business is the $84.4M of adjusted revenue. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The headline profit is mostly a paper gain
takeaways.text: A $598.4M non-cash gain from revaluing the digital assets Bullish holds — versus an $11.4M loss a year ago — is bigger than the entire $576.3M net income. Strip out the mark-to-market swings and adjusted net income was $18.7M, up 36%.

takeaways.title: The underlying business is growing
takeaways.text: Adjusted revenue rose 10% to $84.4M and adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $35.6M, a 42% margin, as subscription, services and other revenue grew 13%. Adjusted transaction revenue was $28.0M, up from $26.7M.

takeaways.title: Buyback authorized, Equiniti deal on track
takeaways.text: Bullish's board authorized a $300M share repurchase program, and the Equiniti acquisition — the deal that would put Bullish into tokenized equities — is expected to close in January 2027. Digital asset sales fell 23% to $32.1B in a weaker market.

oneTimers: A $598.4M non-cash gain from the change in fair value of digital assets held (vs an $11.4M loss in Q3 2025) is the main reason GAAP net income of $576.3M dwarfs adjusted net income of $18.7M.

A $96.9M loss on the change in fair value of derivatives (vs $5.5M a year ago) and an $82.7M gain on investments in financial assets (vs $55.0M) also swung with crypto markets and are excluded from Bullish's adjusted figures.

Share-based payment expenses were $44.6M in the first nine months of 2026 ($15.6M employee awards plus $29.0M other awards) — a real cost that Bullish's adjusted net income and adjusted EBITDA both set aside.
footerNote: Bullish reports under IFRS. Nearly all of its $32.1B of reported revenue is digital-asset sales passed straight through to customers — the business it actually keeps is the $84.4M of adjusted revenue (non-IFRS).
